---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Broad Sample Worst Year Charge Coverage
EXPRESSION: RATIO(SUB(TS_MIN(COALESCE(oancf, ADD(ib, dp)), 3), ADD(xint, dvt)), ADD(ABS(TS_MIN(COALESCE(oancf, ADD(ib, dp)), 3)), ADD(ADD(xint, dvt), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Recurring claims must be met in bad years as well as good ones, and the internal cash available to meet them is the same economic quantity whether reported on the cash-flow statement or approximated by income plus depreciation; the firm whose weakest recent year still cleared interest and dividends is the one with genuine, unconditional financial autonomy.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Two design choices have each independently strengthened this mechanism in evaluation — the worst-year cash-flow input (dividend version: alpha 5.4%, t=4.20, Sharpe 0.62) and the COALESCE sample extension (fmb 3.75, t_alpha 4.00 at 0.126 coverage versus 0.080) — and they operate on different parts of the construct, one on the statistic and one on the sample. Combining them in the final round is the natural consolidation: the tail treatment supplies the economics and the broader sample supplies the estimation precision that has capped ls_talpha across this archive.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Surplus After Commitments And Asset Replacement
EXPRESSION: RATIO(SUB(SUB(MA(oancf, 3), ADD(xint, dvt)), MA(dp, 3)), ADD(ABS(MA(oancf, 3)), ADD(ADD(ADD(xint, dvt), MA(dp, 3)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Cash left after interest and dividends overstates true discretionary surplus for capital-intensive firms, because a portion must be reinvested simply to replace worn-out assets; deducting depreciation as the maintenance requirement identifies firms whose surplus is genuinely free rather than already owed to the asset base.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Every commitment-coverage construct in this archive treats creditors and shareholders as the only claimants on cash, which systematically flatters heavy-asset firms whose reported coverage evaporates once replacement investment is funded. Adding the maintenance claim is new economic content rather than a rescaling, and it should sharpen the long leg by removing capital-intensive firms that currently score well on the champion but have no real freedom of action.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Market Dependence Per Unit Of Internal Capacity
EXPRESSION: WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(ABS(MA(oancf, 3)), ADD(ADD(xint, dvt), 1))), 1)
HYPOTHESIS: What makes external capital raising informative is not its size relative to the balance sheet but its size relative to the firm's own capacity to fund itself; a dollar raised by a firm generating ten dollars of cash after commitments is routine treasury activity, while the same dollar raised by a firm with no internal capacity is a dependency.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The archive's best short-side result required a MIN conjunction of shortfall and issuance (alpha -5.1%, t=-4.09), which discards information in the middle of the distribution and produces a lumpier sort; deflating issuance by internal funding capacity expresses the same forced-financing idea as a single continuous variable that should improve the Fama-MacBeth slope while retaining the portfolio spread. It also differs from the published external-financing anomaly precisely in the deflator, which is a cross-theme quantity rather than a size proxy.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Consolidated Autonomy And Capital Return Score
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(MA(oancf, 3), ADD(xint, dvt)), ADD(ABS(MA(oancf, 3)), ADD(ADD(xint, dvt), 1))), SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at)), RATIO(prstkc, ADD(at, 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: The theme's complete story has three observable components — the firm covers its recurring claims from operations, it takes nothing from the capital markets, and it voluntarily returns cash through the discretionary channel — and a firm satisfying all three is the clearest case of underpriced cash generation, while its opposite is the clearest case of concealed funding need.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Each channel has been validated separately in this archive (coverage: alpha 6.7%; coverage plus financing restraint: 4.5% with fmb 3.28; rigid-claim safety plus buybacks: 4.9% with Sharpe 0.60), but no construct has held all three simultaneously, and the buyback leg in particular carried independent information that the two-channel version omits. Rank-summing keeps every leg continuous so both tails stay populated, which is the property that made the two-channel composite outperform the MIN conjunctions on Sharpe.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Broad Sample Persistent Coverage Regime
EXPRESSION: MA(RATIO(SUB(COALESCE(oancf, ADD(ib, dp)), ADD(xint, dvt)), ADD(ABS(COALESCE(oancf, ADD(ib, dp))), ADD(ADD(xint, dvt), 1))), 5)
HYPOTHESIS: Structural financial slack is revealed by a firm holding comfortable coverage of its recurring claims year after year, and that regime should be measurable across the full universe of reporting firms rather than only those with modern cash-flow statements.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The five-year average of the fully formed coverage state produced alpha 5.4% with Sharpe 0.56 on the narrow sample, and the sample extension independently raised fmb to 3.75 and t_alpha to 4.00; pairing regime persistence with breadth tests whether the archive's recurring precision ceiling was a sample-size artifact. Paired with Signal 1, this also discriminates whether the durable component of the mechanism is best captured by the floor or by the average of the coverage regime, which is the last open design question in this family.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Coverage Of Recurring And Maturing Claims
EXPRESSION: RATIO(SUB(SUB(MA(oancf, 3), ADD(xint, dvt)), dlc), ADD(ABS(MA(oancf, 3)), ADD(ADD(ADD(xint, dvt), dlc), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: A firm needs nothing from any capital provider only when its operating cash covers interest, the dividend, and the principal falling due within the year; measures that omit one class overstate autonomy for firms that are quietly rolling maturities or quietly under-distributing.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The two obligation sets have each produced strong standalone evidence — maturing principal (alpha 5.2%, t=3.68) and recurring charges (alpha 6.7%, t=4.16) — and their union has never actually been evaluated, so the final round should settle whether the claims carry complementary information or whether the recurring-charge version already subsumes the maturity calendar. The answer determines which obligation definition future work should adopt, and if complementary the union should deliver the archive's largest and most reliable spread.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---CRITIQUE Broad Sample Worst Year Charge Coverage---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: A defensible consolidation of two independently validated design choices (downside-tail cash input and the COALESCE sample extension) that carries a distinct economic claim about bad-year autonomy rather than a pure rescaling, though it remains an incremental merge of archive variants and inherits the family's implicit double-count of interest (oancf is already net of interest paid).

---CRITIQUE Surplus After Commitments And Asset Replacement---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Deducting depreciation as a maintenance claim is genuinely new economic content for this family, but note that oancf minus dp collapses toward accrual earnings, so the signal risks partially reducing to a standard earnings-to-assets profitability measure rather than isolating discretionary surplus.

---CRITIQUE Market Dependence Per Unit Of Internal Capacity---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Issuance deflated by internal cash capacity is close to a monotone re-expression of the already-tested "Internal Funding Share Of Total Capital" (both are essentially functions of issuance/|oancf|), and it also sits squarely on top of the published net-external-financing anomaly, so the only difference is the addition of xint+dvt to the denominator — a cosmetic change.

---CRITIQUE Consolidated Autonomy And Capital Return Score---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: A coherent three-leg composite of separately validated channels, but it is close to a kitchen-sink assembly of archive winners with an unacknowledged implicit weighting (nesting gives coverage 50% and each other leg 25%), so any improvement will be hard to attribute and prone to archive-fitting.

---CRITIQUE Broad Sample Persistent Coverage Regime---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is the archive's "Persistent Fixed Charge Coverage Regime" with the input series swapped for the already-tested COALESCE variant — a pure sample-extension rediscovery with no new economic content, and it duplicates the same tweak proposed in Signal 1.

---CRITIQUE Coverage Of Recurring And Maturing Claims---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The union of recurring charges and maturing principal has not in fact been evaluated and the test question is well posed, though the construct mixes a stock (dlc) with flows and is likely to load heavily on a short-debt/leverage tilt already captured by the two parent signals.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Self Funded Expansion
EXPRESSION: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(MA(oancf, 3), ADD(xint, dvt)), ADD(ABS(MA(oancf, 3)), ADD(ADD(xint, dvt), 1))), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(TREND(RATIO(sale, at), 5), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: A firm that is expanding its revenue per dollar of assets while still covering interest and dividends entirely from operations is compounding without any help from capital markets; growth financed internally is durable, whereas the market treats growth as uniformly capital-hungry and therefore underprices the firms that need no funding to achieve it.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: Every conjunction tested in this archive paired funding autonomy with a financing action — payout, buybacks, or issuance — and none paired it with operating expansion, so this asks a genuinely different question: whether autonomy is most valuable where the business is actually growing rather than where it is harvesting. It also addresses the main economic weakness of the coverage family, which tends to select mature, low-growth cash cows, by requiring the long leg to be growing as well as self-financing.
REASONING: Both legs are continuous industry z-scores built from widely reported items, so coverage should remain in the archive's 0.08 range with no point masses.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Accumulated Five Year Retained Surplus
EXPRESSION: WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(SUB(oancf, ADD(xint, dvt)), 5), ADD(at, 1)), 1)
HYPOTHESIS: What ultimately matters is the stock of cash a business has generated and kept after paying all recurring claims over a full cycle, relative to the assets employed; that accumulated surplus is the raw material for future distributions and acquisitions, and its magnitude — not merely the sign of a coverage ratio — is what the market fails to extrapolate.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio
REASONING: Every strong signal in this family uses a bounded self-normalizing ratio that compresses magnitude, so a firm clearing its charges by a hair scores nearly as high as one clearing them tenfold; the sales-deflated version that preserved magnitude delivered alpha 4.8% with t=3.75, confirming that scale information is being discarded. Cumulating five years of post-commitment surplus against the current asset base is a stock rather than a rate concept and is not a time-average of the archived ratio, which makes it a distinct statistic rather than an input or window swap.
REASONING: Five-year cumulation also averages out lumpy dividend and interest years without the smoothing-then-ratio distortion that the archive's MA-based constructs carry.
